openings.claim: Location uncertainty is a plausible contributor to delayed correct-hold pickups, but the synthetic stipulations do not establish its cause or justify continuous location upkeep.
openings.delta: Prioritize a bounded cause-discrimination probe before choosing availability messaging, record upkeep, or cart storage as the intervention.
openings.prediction: Delayed encounters will disproportionately include stale location entries or household-name mismatches, including outside the concentrated demand interval.
openings.rival_prediction: Peak demand is the main driver: pickups with accurate locations will still exceed two minutes during the concentrated interval, while second searches explain little delay after accounting for waiting.
openings.defeat: Encounter-linked records show that stale locations and household-name mismatches rarely explain second searches or excess time, while accurate-location pickups remain delayed chiefly by waiting.
openings.probe: The existing clerk uses the existing timing sheet behind the desk to sample ordinary pickups, distinguishing waiting from retrieval time and noting second-search reason, location accuracy, arrival recency, and cart load. Verify the correct reader before every handoff. Use only the existing shelves, cart, paper, and pencils. Cap all daily preparation and upkeep at ten clerk-minutes; stop optional recording when that cap cannot be maintained. Evaluate diagnostic feasibility and association, not intervention efficacy.
assumptions: The clerk can capture sufficiently informative encounter notes within remaining preparation capacity without materially slowing handoffs.
The sample includes enough variation in demand and storage conditions to distinguish the rival explanations.

decision: Converge on bounded diagnosis as the next step. Its feasibility remains unverified; no eventual intervention is established. Preserve prompt, correct, private pickup for readers and the evening clerk, and retain the 95% within-two-minutes target with no wrong-reader handoffs.

unresolved.issue: Availability certainty may matter, but interview representativeness and any benefit remain unverified.
Cart speed may reflect recency or load; it does not establish a storage advantage.
Eight preparation minutes plus six correction minutes do not demonstrate compliance with the ten-minute allowance.
